title: Inclusion-Exclusion OQ-03: Zeta and Möbius Transforms
description: Formalizes the algebraic structure of inclusion-exclusion via Zeta/Möbius transforms on the subset lattice. Proves Möbius inversion μ∘ζ = id. Connects to fast subset convolution (O(n·2ⁿ) algorithm). 14 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: The Möbius function of the subset lattice gives the inclusion-exclusion principle its algebraic meaning. Möbius inversion (Rota, 1964) generalizes PIE to arbitrary posets. The fast subset convolution algorithm (Björklund-Husfeldt-Kaski-Koivisto, 2007) computes Möbius transforms in O(n·2ⁿ).
overview.problemStatement: Formalize the Zeta and Möbius transforms on 2^[n] and prove Möbius inversion μ∘ζ = id, revealing PIE as Möbius inversion on the subset lattice.
overview.proofStrategy: Define zetaTransform: (ζf)(S) = Σ_{T⊆S} f(T) and mobiusTransform: (μg)(S) = Σ_{T⊆S} (-1)^|S\T| g(T). Prove cancellation via signed inclusion-exclusion of subsets.
keyInsights: **PIE = Möbius inversion**: the inclusion-exclusion formula is exactly Möbius inversion on the boolean lattice 2^[n], where μ(T,S) = (-1)^{|S\T|}.
**Algorithmic efficiency**: naive computation of ζf or μg costs O(3^n) (iterate over pairs T⊆S); fast subset sum (SOS) achieves O(n·2^n) using dimension-by-dimension processing.
**Duality**: ζ and μ are inverses — knowing either transform determines the other, giving a 'change of basis' between pointwise and cumulative representations.

conclusion.summary: 14 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Möbius inversion on the subset lattice proved, giving the algebraic foundation of inclusion-exclusion.
conclusion.implications: The Möbius inversion perspective on PIE connects combinatorics to algebraic number theory and explains why many counting formulas have an inclusion-exclusion structure.
openQuestions: Can Rota's generalized Möbius inversion be proved for arbitrary finite posets?
Can the fast subset sum algorithm be verified as computing the Möbius transform?
Can the Dedekind zeta function be connected to Möbius inversion on divisibility lattices?
